support_text: In the human BBB co-culture model, vectorial transport of [3H]indinavir over 60 min showed a basal‐to‐apical flux 1.5‐times higher than the apical‐to‐basal flux. Pretreatment with 5 µM quinidine (a P‐gp modulator) significantly increased apical‐to‐basal transport (flux twice that without quinidine) and nearly quadrupled intracellular accumulation (from 7.5±0.3 to 30±2 pmol mg−1 protein), consistent with P‐gp‐mediated efflux inhibited by quinidine.
In humans, the ratio of hydroxyurea concentrations in the cerebrospinal fluid to serum was measured as 0.20 ± 0.07.
In rats, levetiracetam administration at a dose of 40 mg kg−1 resulted in an extracellular fluid/serum Cmax ratio of 3.2 in the frontal cortex.
In the ADMET profiling of novel marine analogs, Obatoclax was reported to have a BBB value of 0.6766.
Following treatment with the CDG system in mice, the tissue to serum drug concentration ratio (T/S) for the brain was 3.0 at 30 min.

In LLC-PK1-mMdr1a cells (overexpressing mouse Abcb1a), the permeability of seliciclib was much greater in the basolateral-to-apical direction than apical-to-basolateral, resulting in an efflux ratio (ER) of 15.31 ± 3.54, compared to 1.44 ± 0.10 in control LLC-PK1-mock cells. Co-incubation with the Abcb1a-specific inhibitor LY335979 reduced the ER in LLC-PK1-mMdr1a cells to 1.05 ± 0.25, while the ER in mock cells remained unchanged (1.21 ± 0.33).

In Caco-2 cells, the efflux ratio (Papp BL-to-AP / Papp AP-to-BL) of CD was 71. In the presence of GF120918 (2 µM), a P-gp specific inhibitor, the efflux ratio decreased to 16, indicating P-gp-mediated efflux. Cyclosporin A (25 µM) reduced the ratio to 5.6.
The efflux ratio (ER) for diazepam in MDCKII-MDR1 cells was 0.84.
Compound 10 demonstrated moderate to low P-gp efflux as measured in Madin-Darby canine kidney cells transfected with human MDR1 gene (MDCK-MDR1 ER = 5.4).

In Table 2 (paragraph 13), compound 20 showed a Pgp/BCRP permeability ratio of 5.0 and a passive permeability of 84 nm/s in MDCKII-MDR1 cells double-transduced with BCRP. According to the accompanying text (paragraph 16), none of the compounds in Table 2 was a significant Pgp/BCRP efflux transporter substrate.
Acebutolol demonstrates a CSF/plasma ratio of 0.11, indicating it penetrates into the cerebrospinal fluid to a greater extent than diacetolol.

In P-gp knockout rats, the unbound brain-to-plasma partition coefficient (Kp,uu) of seletalisib was 0.44, compared to ca. 0.09 in wild-type rats and cynomolgus monkeys. This increase in brain distribution demonstrates that P-gp restricts seletalisib brain exposure. Kp,uu was maintained low over a range of doses (7.5 to 750 mg/kg). The study concludes seletalisib is an avid P-gp substrate.
Cyclic secondary amine analogue 14c displayed reasonably good brain penetration (B/P) in rats, with a B/P ratio of 0.3 reported in Table 2.
The apparent permeability coefficient (Papp) of K-604 across the BBB was 21.9 x 10^-6 cm/s in the in vitro BBB Kit evaluation system.
The Kp,brain value for ALT after oral administration was 2.34 ± 0.63 in zebrafish and 0.19 ± 0.05 in mouse.
Compound 25, characterized by high efflux ratios, demonstrated limited brain penetration, with a Kp,uu of 0.014 in rat brain exposure studies.
Compound 2, a γ-carboline, has a reported B/P ratio of 0.75.
In Table 3, compound 9a shows an efflux ratio of 1.4 in stably expressed human MDR1 P-glycoprotein in MDCK cells, indicating minimal P-gp-mediated efflux.
Using a full PBPK model and the corrected Poulin and Theil method, the predicted brain tissue partition coefficient (Kp) for Buprenorphine was 3.41.
Using dual probe in vivo microdialysis, Entacapone exhibited a brain/blood ratio of 0.14 ± 0.11.
Biodistribution studies in mice revealed brain uptake of [3H] epibatidine at 11.5% ID/g tissue at 30 min p.i.
The CSF to serum concentration ratio of lamotrigine in rats rises to a steady-state value of 0.62.
Preliminary data indicate that normal values of the rubidium extraction fraction (E_R) are approximately 0.025.
(-)-epicatechin rapidly crossed the blood-brain barrier within 20 minutes after iv administration, with a calculated brain distribution ratio (AUCbrain/AUCblood) of 0.1065 ± 0.0531 in rats.
In Caco-2 cells, compound 1v had a Papp of 19×10-6 cm/s and an efflux ratio of 0.5, indicating no significant efflux transport.
In patients with neurosurgical disorders, the concentration ratio (k) of primidone between brain and plasma was 0.9.
In vivo positron emission tomography (PET) studies in conscious macaques showed that [11C]-mecamylamine had a thalamus uptake value of 0.258% ID/(kg mL).
The virtual calculation of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability for compound 3f was reported as 0.09 using the pre-ADMET in silico tool.
The P-gp susceptibility of compound 1 was evaluated using human MDR1-transfected LLC-PK1 cell monolayers, yielding a transcellular transport ratio ((B-to-A)/(A-to-B)) of 2.4.

It has been reported that amantadine has high penetrative activity into the brain after infusion in rats, where the brain concentration of amantadine was 16-fold higher than the free concentration in serum.
CPD37 was identified as a brain penetrant small molecule inhibitor of ELOVL1 and exhibited a brain to plasma ratio of 1.1.
Compound 4o in an MDR1 bidirectional transport assay exhibited an efflux ratio (B→A/A→B) of 2.1.
AZD9272 has good brain exposure (brain to plasma ratio = 1) and long half-life (t1/2 ~ 2.5 hours) after an oral dose of 3 µg/kg in rat.

At 8 µM racemic verapamil in D3-treated Caco-2 cells, the Papp(b-a)/Papp(a-b) efflux ratios were 1.9±0.2 for both R- and S-verapamil. This efflux was completely abolished by the Pgp inhibitor GF120918, indicating that verapamil is a substrate of P-glycoprotein (P-gp).

Colchicine (0.1 mM) showed polarized transport across Caco-2 cell monolayers with an efflux ratio (Papp BL-AP / Papp AP-BL) of 20.7, indicating P-gp-mediated efflux. The efflux ratio was reduced in a concentration-dependent manner by the known P-gp inhibitors verapamil (to 13.9, 8.2, and 5.1 at 10, 50, 100 µM) and quinidine (to 14.0, 9.5, and 5.5 at the same concentrations).
In pharmacokinetic studies in male Sprague-Dawley rats, compound 36 showed a brain-to-plasma ratio (B/Pc) of 1.
Brain and plasma levels were also measured 12 hours after dose administration, following chronic (28 days) treatment. The brain/plasma ratio of AM6545 remained low (i.e., 0.07).
Using Caco-2 cell monolayers, the efflux ratio (ER) of risperidone (RIS) was 3.3, which is more than 2, indicating that RIS is a substrate of P-glycoprotein (P-gp).
Hederagenin, identified as an active component of Huangqi, Sanleng, and Ezhu in the TCMSP database, has a BBB value of 0.96.
In brain homogenates from healthy rhesus macaques (NHPs), niraparib showed a mean Kp, brain of 3.179 as measured by LC-MS/MS bioanalysis.

In Caco-2 cell monolayers, treatment with 500 µM 1-monoolein significantly reduced the basolateral-to-apical efflux of Rh123 (7.9 ± 0.8 ×106 cm/s) compared to the untreated control (21.1 ± 2.9 ×106 cm/s, P<0.05), indicating that 1-monoolein inhibits P-gp.

In Caco-2 cell monolayers, the B→A apparent permeability of PTX at 180 min was 19.43 ± 0.86 ×10^-6 cm/s without inhibitor, and decreased to 5.12 ± 0.87 ×10^-6 cm/s in the presence of 5 µM compound 19 (P < 0.05), indicating inhibition of P-gp-mediated efflux transport.
Ortataxel (T-35) showed asymmetric transport across Caco-2 monolayers with an efflux ratio of 6.84, indicating it is a P-gp substrate.
Compound 55 showed an efflux ratio (ER) of 15, which suggested limited brain penetration.
Chronic delivery of caffeine at 0.3 g/L through drinking water in mice achieved moderate levels of caffeine (about 4 µM) in both plasma and brain, with a reported plasma:brain ratio close to 1.

In CF1 mdr1a (+/+) mice, the brain AUC0-4h/plasma AUC0-4h ratio for TMZ was 0.349, while in mdr1a (-/-) knockout mice it was 0.383 (p<0.05), demonstrating increased brain exposure in the absence of P-glycoprotein. The authors concluded that TMZ is strongly likely an ABCB1 substrate at the BBB.
In patients with an intact blood-brain barrier, urate is excluded from the cerebral compartment, with a CSF/serum concentration ratio of approximately 0.14 in controls.
In conscious rats, [14C]urea showed a k1 value of 8.5 × 10-5 s-1 in the pons during iv bolus injection analysis.

Alpidem is a weak base and poorly ionized at physiological pH, which permits its diffusion through the blood-brain barrier and lipid-rich membranes. In rats, alpidem has a rate of entry into the CNS (BUI) of 0.71.
At 48 hours after the start of the IV MTX infusion, the median CSF MTX level was 2.0 × 10−6 M.
All cationic diamidines examined, including pentamidine, showed high B/P ratios (ranging from 23 for pentamidine up to 114 for DB829), suggesting good CNS penetration.

In a child with meningo-encaphalitis and tuberculous rhombo-encephalitis, the CSF penetration of rifampicin was extremely poor compared with plasma Cmax, with a CSF:plasma ratio of 0.04 and a CSF Cmax of 1.4 mg/mL measured 2 hours post-infusion.

Using Discovery Studio (DS) to calculate ADMET descriptors, cinnamyl alcohol (CALC) showed a BBB value of 1, which falls within the range that describes a drug candidate (where a drug should not cross BBB level 3).
In a mouse neuroPK study, compound 30 demonstrated modest brain permeability with an unbound brain (Cb,u) to unbound plasma (Cp,u) concentration ratio of 0.2.
In overdose fatalities from the Forensic Tox Division, Florence (1990–2005), the mean brain/blood ratio for benzoylecgonine was 0.67 ± 0.47.
In human samples, N8 exhibited a CSF-to-plasma ratio value of 0.17.
Compound 27 showed an apparent permeability (A→B) of 8.5 x 10^-6 cm/s and an efflux ratio of 1.6 in hMDR1-LLC-PK1 cells, indicating low efflux (non-substrate for MDR1/P-gp).
The brain-to-plasma partition coefficient of elacridar was dramatically enhanced to 3.5 in MDR1a/b(-/-) mice, indicating that both P-gp and BCRP limit the brain distribution of elacridar.
In conscious rhesus macaques, the brain/plasma ratio for telmisartan at 60 min was 0.13, as determined by PET imaging.
In community-acquired meningitis patients, the vancomycin concentration in CSF was 2.47 ± 1.15 mg/L and the CSF-to-serum ratio was 0.26 ± 0.12.
In rats, the concentration ratio of metoprolol in the brain versus plasma is 6.
The predicted BBB permeability for compound 10d was 100.00.
CMs significantly enhanced the accumulation of coumarin-6 in brain, and the Cmax of CMs in brain was 4.74% of injected dose/g tissue (ID/g).
In rabbits treated with a combination of oral lead and zinc for 4 weeks, the cerebrum/blood ratio for lead was 0.2.

Bidirectional transport of ticagrelor across Caco-2 monolayer showed a mean efflux ratio of 2.71, with higher efflux permeability than influx. Co-incubation with the P-gp inhibitor valspodar decreased the efflux Papp from 1.60 × 10^-5 cm/s to 1.13 × 10^-5 cm/s and reduced the efflux ratio by 70%, indicating P-gp-mediated active transport.
In adult rats fed, the brain/blood ratio of glucose was 0.22 ± 0.01.

Compound 17 appeared to be a Pgp substrate as judged by the efflux ratio (ER) in LLC-PK1 cells overexpressed with human P-glycoprotein, with an ER of 8.6 (versus 1.1 in parental cells and 7.8 in rat P-gp overexpressing cells) as shown in Table 3.

[14C]Rovatirelin (10 µmol/L) across Caco-2 cell monolayers showed an efflux ratio of 2.8 (Table 4). Co-addition of the BCRP inhibitors novobiocin (50 µmol/L) or Ko143 (1 µmol/L) did not significantly reduce the efflux ratio (2.6 and 3.3, with inhibition ratios of 6.2% and -17.1%, respectively), indicating rovatirelin is not a BCRP substrate.
Using a blood/brain partition coefficient of 33 calculated by Timchalk et al. (2002) for chlorpyrifos in rats, brain concentrations would be estimated to range from 0.33-3.3 nM.
PET imaging in mice showed that [18F]MeTz demonstrated better BBB penetration than [18F]HTz, with a Cmax/Cmin ratio of 5.6, possibly due to increased lipophilicity.
For intact diazepam, equilibrium between plasma and brain appeared essentially complete within 1-3 min after the injection, with an overall mean (±SE) brain:plasma concentration ratio of 1.99(±0.12).

In bovine olfactory mucosa, the secretory (submucosal-to-mucosal) flux of etoposide was significantly greater than the mucosal-to-submucosal flux, with an efflux ratio of 2.02. This directional transport was inhibited by the P-gp inhibitors quinidine (1 mM) and 2,4-dinitrophenol (1 mM), confirming that etoposide is a P-gp substrate.
The ratio (r) between brain and concomitant plasma AUC values was 0.012 after treatment with paclitaxel in healthy mice.
In healthy adult pigs, the AUCtissue/AUCplasma ratio for ganciclovir in the subcortical ECF after the first dose was 0.42, determined by microdialysis.
In adult guinea pigs, the brain to free plasma concentration ratio for triamterene was about 0.1, with individual values of 0.065, 0.082, and 0.09 reported for the first three animals.
In awake rats, the unidirectional incorporation coefficient (k*) for [1-14C]Docosahexaenoate was 3.08±0.14 x 10^4 cm^3*s^-1*g brain^-1 under control conditions.
Bidirectional transport of irinotecan gave a cER of 3.2 in MDCKII cells (no suppression), indicating hABCG2-mediated efflux.

In Caco-2 cell monolayers, after the P-gp inhibitor verapamil (300 µM), the AP-BL Papp of phillyrin (2.2 µg/ml) greatly increased from 7.15×10−6 to 39.90×10−6 cm/s and BL-AP transportation decreased from 7.35×10−6 to 4.08×10−6 cm/s, with the efflux ratio decreasing from 1.028 to 0.102, implying that P-gp might be involved in the efflux of phillyrin.
The metabolite 4-HPPH demonstrated poor blood-brain-barrier permeability in rats, with an average brain/plasma ratio of 0.06 ± 0.01 following intravenous administration.
Compound 5L had a predicted CNS permeability (log PS) of -2.15, determined through in silico ADMET profiling.
Morphine had a Pgp effect of 1.24 ± 0.08, defined as the ratio of brain uptake clearance in mdr1a(-/-) mice to that in mdr1a(+/+) mice during in situ perfusion.
Compound 3 showed an MDR BA/AB efflux ratio of 1.55 ± 0.7 in MDR1-transfected MDCK cells at 1 µM, as determined by MS-based quantification of apparent permeability from the table and footnote.

Following intravenous administration in male Sprague-Dawley rats, the ratio of the area under the cocaine concentration-time curve (AUC) between the olfactory bulb and plasma up to 2 min post dose was 6.16 ± 0.94.

The most promising LAT1-targeting inhibitors (probenecid derivatives) significantly increased the permeability of vinblastine across the rat blood-brain barrier, doubling its brain uptake rate. These inhibitors can inhibit MRP, indicating that MRP efflux limits vinblastine brain exposure, making vinblastine an MRP substrate at the BBB.
MA levels in the brain increased approximately 20-fold in Mdr1a-/- mice after oral administration of 0.2 mg/kg MA, compared to wild-type FVB mice (P < 0.05).
The more hydrophilic compound 24 exhibited an unacceptably high efflux ratio of 6.6 in the MDCK efflux assay (presumably measuring P-gp transport).

In a patient treated with atenolol, drug levels in serum and CSF, determined by high-performance liquid chromatography, were 20 ng/ml and 10 ng/ml, respectively, which corresponds to a serum/CSF ratio of 2 as noted in the subsequent discussion.
In vivo studies with mdr1a +/+ and -/- CF-1 mice confirmed the lack of P-gp interaction for CDPPB (30m) and indicated it was brain penetrant with a normalized brain to plasma AUC ratio of 1.7.
In the compound summary table, M4K2149 is reported with a Caco-2 efflux ratio of 8.1, indicating directional transport in this assay.
Acenocoumarol was considered a weak substrate of P-gp with an ER of 1.5.
In rats, the brain/serum quotient for hexobarbital was 0.494 ± 0.028 following an infusion of 15 mg/kg per min for 3 min under saline control conditions.

After injection of 20 MBq [11C]D617 we observed a very low brain uptake and a homogeneous distribution of radioactivity in control rats (<0.1% ID/g). After treatment with the P-gp inhibitor tariquidar, brain radioactivity increased up to 3-fold. These data indicate that [11C]D617 is a weak P-gp substrate.
Indomethacin had an observed Kp,uu,cell of 0.60, determined using brain homogenate and brain slice methods.
In children receiving dexamethasone therapy, the mean CSF/serum ratio for ceftriaxone in Group 3 (receiving combination therapy) was 0.12 ± 0.07.

In patients with serious nosocomial infections, moxalactam levels in the cerebrospinal fluid were measured 4 hours after the last dose. For one patient with noninflamed meninges, the percentage ratio of body fluid level to serum level was 1.0, with a CSF level of 26 µg/ml.
In the postnatal stress group of rats at age P30, the Evans blue ic was 0.333 ± 0.006 mL.
Compound 3e was predicted via the pkCSM database to have a low potential to reach the CNS, with a logPS value of -3.20.

L-[123I]iodo-1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-7-hydroxyisoquinoline-3-carboxylic acid (ITIC) passed the blood-brain barrier and thereafter showed efflux from the brain. Following intravenous injection, the radioactivity concentration in healthy rat brain 15 min p.i. was 0.07% ID/g.
In a rat plasma/brain level (PBL) cassette assay, NAM 28d exhibited a Kp,uu of 0.29.
The Kp,brain value for Dexamethasone was 0.70 in P-gp knockout (-/-) mice.

In a table summarizing in vitro studies, racemic talinolol at 100 µM in Caco-2 cells showed an apical-to-basal permeability of 1.9 × 10−7 cm/s and a basal-to-apical permeability of 14 × 10−7 cm/s, giving an efflux ratio of 7.4. IC50 values for various inhibitors of the basal-to-apical transport are also listed.
Pgp-deficient mice have similar hydroxyzine brain-to-free plasma concentration ratios (ratios of ... 236 after 60 min).

Digoxin (5 µM) exhibited an efflux ratio of 5.1 across Caco-2 cell monolayers. Co-incubation with the P-gp inhibitor verapamil (100 µM) reduced the efflux ratio to 1.1, confirming that digoxin is a P-glycoprotein substrate.

In rats orally treated with tanshinone IIA (TSA) at 5 mg/kg alone, the brain-to-plasma AUC ratio (Ri) was 0.31. When TSA was co-administered with oral quinidine at 50 mg/kg, the brain Ri increased to 0.77, demonstrating enhanced brain exposure through P-glycoprotein inhibition.
Following i.v. administration in rats, 3,4-dehydrochlorambucil showed a mean brain:plasma concentration integral ratio of 0.
It has been reported that the concentration of cefepime in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) could reach 10% of its concentration in plasma.

Permeability of AAI across LLC-PK1-BCRP cell monolayers in the presence of BCRP inhibitors. At 20 µM AAI, the net efflux ratio was 3.0, which is lower than the 13.8 seen without inhibitors, demonstrating that BCRP-mediated transport is inhibited.
In the baseline measurement (group I) conducted on Wistar rats, the mean cerebellum/blood ratio for 99mTc-HMPAO was 1.06 (SD 0.21).
Molnupiravir was detectable in the striatum with a low penetration ratio (AUCbrain/AUCblood) of 0.005 ± 0.001.
Compound 60 was reported to have a brain/plasma ratio of 0.08.

In MDCKII cells overexpressing hMDR1, there was an active apically directed transport with a transport ratio of 3.2, which was completely blocked by zosuquidar, indicating that CYT387 is a clear transport substrate of hMDR1.
In 16-month-old WT mice, paliperidone exhibited a Kp,uu,brain of 0.108.
In rats, lorlatinib showed a CSF/Plasma Ratio or Brain/Plasma Ratio of 0.6 for AUC0-24h.

For ZINC2005305, the blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability score of − 0.931 indicates that the compound is unlikely to penetrate the BBB, and P-glycoprotein substrate and inhibitor predictions are negative.
In vitro study indicates that mouse Abcg2 modestly transports galunisertib with an efflux ratio of 3.1.
Compound 50 (2-aminoquinoline) showed a modest P-gp efflux ratio of 3.1 in a bidirectional permeability assay [230].

In LLC-PK1 cells expressing human ABCB1 wild-type (ABCB1wt), aripiprazole showed an efflux ratio of 6.04 ± 0.24. Co-treatment with GF120918 (10 nM) reduced it to 1.52 ± 0.19, confirming P-gp-mediated efflux. Cellular accumulation in ABCB1wt cells was 235.2 ± 12.6 nM, significantly less than control (542.6 ± 15.4 nM).
The brain uptake index (BUI) for glycine during initial circulatory uptake in rats was 2.5.
M1 had a net efflux ratio of 32 in MDCKII cells overexpressing P-gp, normalized for efflux in wild-type MDCKII cells, as shown in Table 1 (p. 37).
Compound 8c showed an efflux ratio of 2.6 across the MDR1-MDCK cell line.
Masuoka and Hansson showed that intravenous administration of 14C-labeled propranolol is rapidly taken up by the rat brain and concentrated 50 times greater in the brain than in the blood.

In Caco-2 cell monolayers, addition of MK571 (a known MRP inhibitor) significantly increased the AP-to-BL transport of morroniside (25 µM) with no effect on BL-to-AP transport, reducing the efflux ratio from 1.61 to 0.40. This indicates that morroniside is effluxed by MRP.
S18986 crosses the BBB intensively, and based on a noncompartmental approach in rats, the Ratio AUC (Brain/Plasma, unbound) in the bECF of the hippocampus was 0.25.
In rats, the brain uptake index (BUI) of nicotine was 165 at 15 seconds after carotid artery injection.
Intravenous administration of ganciclovir to rats resulted in poor penetration into the brain, with a brain-to-blood drug concentration ratio (AUC) of 0.063.
Inhibition of digoxin flux across MDCK-MDR1 monolayers: control efflux ratio 11.26 ± 0.73; with 10 µM mifepristone, efflux ratio reduced to 1.58 ± 0.30.

Table 3 reports that compound 3 has an MDR1 (P-gp) efflux ratio (BA/AB) of 2.3, and paragraph 17 states that it exhibited predicted low-to-moderate P-gp liability and good passive permeability (Papp = 8.4 × 10^-6 cm/s).
Compound 3g had a BBB prediction by Volsurf of -0.35.
In male ddY mice, the brain/blood radioactivity ratio of [11C]4 at 30 min after injection was 3.29 ± 0.37.
Compound 13c was reported to have a Cbr/Cpl ratio of 0.10.
Pgp-mediated transport of vinblastine in LLC-mdr1a cells (with MK571 present) was suppressed by tariquidar (0.2 µM), reducing the cTR from 4.26 to 1.07.
In Table 2, compound 2b showed an MDR efflux ratio of 2.2 in an MDR1-transfected MDCK cell line. No further qualitative statement about P-gp liability is given for this specific analogue.
The fetal brain/maternal plasma Kp ratio for 6β-naltrexol was 15.7 at 120 minutes after injection, indicating rapid entry into the fetal brain.
Following systemic administration (5 mg/kg, i.p.) in mice, the analog compound TG6-10-1 displayed a brain:plasma ratio of 1.6.
The predicted BBB value for Valproic acid was 0.91.
For NFPS, the total brain-to-plasma ratio (Kp,brain) was 0.33 ± 0.04 after a 1 mg/kg infusion over 4 h in rats.
In mice, sulpiride exhibited a Kp,wt of 0.078.
In Table 1, Diazepam showed a Kp,uu,brain of 0.00484 in tg-App ArcSwe mice.
In Caco-2 cells overexpressing human P-gp, tocainide showed a BA/AB efflux ratio of 3.9 (BA=1965 nm/s, AB=496 nm/s), indicating it is a good P-gp substrate.

Compound 5m had an efflux ratio of 90 in Caco-2 monolayer transport, with low A-B permeability (0.5 x 10^-6 cm/s). The authors concluded that efflux ratios >40 indicate these compounds are likely substrates for ABC transporters such as P-glycoprotein.

The BCRP substrate, E3S, exhibited a high efflux ratio (i.e., 48.5) in the VC cells, which was reduced to 10.2 (21% of VC cells) in the BCRP KD cells but remained roughly unchanged in P-gp KD and MRP2 KD cells.
The [S] enantiomer of [11C]-N,α-dimethylbenzylamine (DMBA) was rapidly distributed into the brain in mice, and its estimated distribution volume (DV) in the brain was 6.05.
In the rat brainstem, the concentration of carbon-14-labeled dimethyloxazolidinedione in tissue water relative to plasma water (Ct/Cp) was 0.42.
In silico ADMET properties calculated using DS 3.5 predicted a BBB value of -0.058 for compound 4.
For EAI045, the brain-to-plasma ratio in WT mice was 0.10.

In MDCKII-MRP2 cells, the efflux ratio of forsythiaside was reduced to 1.092 in the presence of the MRP2 inhibitor MK-571, confirming MRP2-mediated efflux. The BL-AP secretion was reduced to 27.2% of control.

Colclough et al. demonstrated in vitro in MDCK cells that osimertinib is a substrate for human BBB efflux transporters (MDR1 (P-gp)/BRCP) with an efflux ratio of 3.2, limiting the brain uptake of this drug.
In biodistribution studies in mice, [18F]19 exhibited a high brain-to-blood ratio of 12.9 at 30 min postinjection.

In bidirectional transport studies across excised rat ileum, talinolol (100 µM) showed an efflux ratio of 3.70 ± 0.24 (B-A Papp 25.30 ± 2.30 vs A-B Papp 6.83 ± 0.26 ×10−6 cm/s). The addition of P-gp inhibitor verapamil (200 µM) or morin (100 µM) significantly reduced the efflux ratio (to 0.30 and 0.50, respectively), confirming that talinolol is a P-gp substrate.

The ratio of basolateral-to-apical efflux to apical-to-basolateral efflux of 1.1 observed in Madin Darby canine kidney cells transfected with the human multidrug resistance 1 gene suggests that linezolid may not be a substrate of P-gp (Pfizer, unpublished data).
Following intracarotid injection in rats, [14C]isopropanol showed a Brain Uptake Index (BUI) at 15 s of 110.0 ±2.0.
The brain tissue/plasma partition coefficient (Kpbr) for 2,2-BPF was calculated to be 6.66 using PK-SIM based on the method of Rodgers and Rowland 2006.
Osimertinib is reported to have a brain/plasma ratio of 3.41.

MDCK-WT cells, which express endogenous canine P-gp, showed polarized efflux of [3H]-vinblastine with a Papp BL-to-AP/Papp AP-to-BL ratio of 15. The P-gp inhibitor GF120918 (2 µM) reduced the ratio to 1.7, and the dual P-gp/MRP2 inhibitor CsA (25 µM) reduced it to 1.1, demonstrating that vinblastine is a substrate of canine P-gp.

In Sprague-Dawley rats with brain tumors, the uptake of gemcitabine was markedly higher in brain tumors than in the tumor-free hemisphere, indicating a more permeable tumor vasculature. The relative brain distribution coefficient in the brain tumor region was 0.186 (approximately 18%).

Following intravenous infusion in rats, only 10% of the free plasma concentration of maraviroc was found in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and 25% in the brain. This limited distribution seems to be due to the affinity of the compound for the efflux transporter P-glycoprotein (Walker et al., 2008).
Spichler and Reed [58] used GC-MS to determine cocaine levels in brain and blood tissues of postmortem cases. In incidental cases, the brain/blood mean ratio for cocaine was 2.5.

In bidirectional transport assays across LLC-PK1 cells stably expressing human ABCB1 wild-type (1199G allele), paroxetine exhibited an efflux ratio (Papp B→A/A→B) of 5.14 ± 0.24, which was reduced to 1.24 ± 0.35 upon co-administration of the P-gp inhibitor LY335979, indicating P-gp-mediated efflux (Table 1, paragraph 40; also described in paragraph 36).

Efflux ratio for digoxin was approximately 10, and transport studies in the presence of the P-gp inhibitor GW918 (1 µM) revealed that P-gp attenuated absorptive transport of digoxin by approximately 8-fold; the apparent Km for P-gp-mediated efflux was >6-fold larger in the absorptive versus secretory direction.

Methotrexate (MTX) showed an unbound brain-to-plasma concentration ratio (Kp,uu) of 0.1 at steady state, indicating limited brain delivery. The paper states that MTX is a substrate of various efflux transporters at the BBB in rats, including multidrug resistance-associated protein 4 (Mrp4/ABCC4), and that this efflux restricts brain penetration.
In MDCK-MDR1 cells, loperamide (1a) showed an efflux ratio of 13 (A→B Papp 0.89 × 10−6 cm s−1, B→A 11.2 × 10−6 cm s−1), confirming that it is a substrate for P-gp-mediated efflux.

In LLC-GA5-COL150 cells overexpressing human P-gp, digoxin (20 nM) showed 19.5-fold higher B-to-A permeability compared to A-to-B, and a CFR of 11.36, while no directional transport was observed in parental LLC-PK1 cells.

In Table 1 (paragraph 36), glycitein showed a pIC50 of 5.99 ± 0.05 for inhibition of BCRP-mediated methotrexate transport in BCRP-expressing membrane vesicles incubated with 100 µM MTX at 37°C for 2 min.

Dabrafenib was a P-gp substrate with an efflux ratio of 36 in MDCKII-hMDR1 cells (paragraph 67). In the presence of the P-gp/BCRP inhibitor GF120918, the efflux ratio of dabrafenib in MDCKII-hMDR1 cells was approximately 1 (paragraph 65), consistent with P-gp-mediated transport.
Acetylsalicylic acid showed a [Brain]/[Blood] concentration ratio of 0.49.

Verapamil was used as an inhibitor of P-gp. When verapamil (100 µM) was added to the donor solution with telmisartan (1.0 µg/mL (1.95 µM)), absorptive permeability of telmisartan increased and secretive one decreased compared to those without verapamil. The permeability ratio was significantly decreased from 13.6 to 1.5 by the addition of verapamil to the donor solution.
Compound 28p was evaluated in a bidirectional MDCK-MDR1 assay for its potential to be a substrate for human P-gp efflux and showed a low efflux ratio of 1.2.

Fluconazole penetrates the cerebrospinal fluid in inflamed and normal meninges. A study in primates receiving fluconazole demonstrated a ratio of area under the cerebrospinal fluid concentration-time curve to area under the plasma concentration-time curve of 0.86.
Meprobamate demonstrated a higher average CSF/blood ratio than any other class of drugs, at approximately 1.0.

measurement_text: L-lysine had a brain uptake index (BUI) of about 16, which is at the lower end of the scale for amino acid brain uptake
support_text: It has been shown by Oldendorf (26) in the rat that essential nutritional amino acids such as L-lysine are taken up more readily than the nonessential. Still, L-lysine has a brain uptake index (BUI) of about 16, belonging to the lower end of the scale for amino acid brain uptake.
In sham-operated control rats administered 10 mg/kg of venlafaxine (Sham-VEN10), the mesencephalon-pons/serum concentration ratio of venlafaxine was 4.0 ± 1.0.

In Caco-2 cell monolayers, co-administration of ketoconazole (500 µM) with saquinavir (1 µM) increased AP→BL permeability (Papp 21.08 ± 4.03 × 10−7 cm/s) and decreased BL→AP permeability (84.9 ± 13.0 × 10−7 cm/s), reducing the efflux ratio to 4.0, indicating inhibition of P-gp-mediated efflux.
Pyrimidine 8 showed a moderately low brain Kp value, which was measured as 0.31 in Table 1.
In the MDCK transport study, log k values were calculated for different rivastigmine formulations. The rivastigmine and NaTC solution exhibited a log k of -1.65 ± 0.06 cm/hour.
In a transcellular transport assay using LLC-MDR1 cells, cimetidine had a corrected transport ratio of 0.5 and was classified as a non‐substrate for P‐gp.
Following an intravenous bolus of the inhibitor PSC-833, quinidine (QND) entered the brain significantly, resulting in an AUCbrain/AUCblood ratio of 134.5.
In female CD2F1/CrlBR mice receiving a 45 s IV infusion of 30 mg/kg cabazitaxel, the brain/plasma exposure ratio was 6.51.

Studies of the transport rate of [3H]-mitoxantrone in WT and elacridar treated (10 µmol L−1) mice revealed that chemical disruption of Bcrp at the BBB significantly increased the entry rate, with an ER_B value of ~3.3 (P < 0.001).
Following the injection of [123I]epidepride into healthy human volunteers, the mean striatum to cerebellum ratio measured by SPET at 180 min after injection was 12.7±1.6.
For baicalein administered at 30 mg kg−1 with cyclosporin A, the AUCbrain/AUCblood ratio was 0.055±0.004.
In Mdr1a knockout rats, verapamil showed a Kp,uu,brain value of 3.4 following cassette dosing.
In WT animals, the brain-to-blood ratio for rapamycin was 0.18, which increased to 5.2 in WT animals treated with the Abcb1/Abcg2 inhibitor elacridar.

In MDCKII-MDR1 cell monolayers (overexpressing human MDR1/P-gp), PF-06282999 exhibited an A-to-B apparent permeability (Papp) of 0.6 ×10^-6 cm/s and a B-to-A Papp of 2.1 ×10^-6 cm/s at pH 7.4, resulting in an efflux ratio of 3.3, indicating that PF-06282999 is a substrate of P-gp.
For human BBB spheroids with a seeding ratio of 1:1:3, the efficient permeability (Pe) of FD4 in 900 µm spheroids was 8.3 ± 1.1 x 10-6 cm s-1 after 4 h of cultivation.
Following i.v. administration in rats, melphalan demonstrated a cerebellum:plasma concentration integral ratio of 0.183.
In a pharmacokinetic study, chitosan-coated SLNs encapsulated sumatriptan, which resulted in a brain sumatriptan deposition of 5.28 µg/g and an AUCbrain/AUCplasma ratio of 4.5.
In rats pretreated with ACTH, the Brain: Plasma ratio of zoxazolamine was reported as 2.9.

In healthy volunteers, after oral administration of 4.5 g of probenecid, the mean concentration of probenecid in the CSF (PCSF) was 9.3 ± 2.9 µg/ml, while the mean plasma concentration (Ppl) was 192 ± 23 µg/ml.
The AUC0-∞ brain-to-plasma ratio after a single 20 mg/kg oral dose of sunitinib was 1.61 in Mdr1a/b(-/-) mice and 0.42 in wild-type mice, supporting that P-gp restricts brain exposure.
In in vitro DMPK assays, PAM 11a proved to be CNS penetrant with a Kp,uu of 0.45.
Selinexor has good CNS penetration with a CSF/plasma ratio of approximately 0.6.

In paragraph 97, the authors report: 'the brain AUC0-24 h in mdr1a(-/-) mice was 6.0-fold higher than the wild-type mice, with a significantly increased brain penetration' and state 'Our results with glabridin as a PgP substrate are consistent with those reported in the literature.' This genetic knockout study provides strong evidence that glabridin is a P-gp substrate.
Compound 9 had an efflux ratio of 5.4 in the MDR1-MDCK bidirectional transport assay (Table 2).

To determine the brain penetrance of ATH-1105, male mice were given a 5 mg/kg intravenous injection. After 10 min, blood and perfused brain tissue were collected, resulting in a plasma concentration of 1,401 ng/mL and a brain concentration of 599 ng/g, which gave a brain to plasma concentration ratio (Kpbrain) of 0.43.
Diazepam was used as a marker of transcellular pathways in the MDCK-MDR1 cell line model mimicking blood-brain barrier permeability.
Following transdermal application of tetramethylpyrazine (TMP), the experimental ratio of drug levels in plasma and brain at 4 hours was 1.34.
Bidirectional transepithelial flux of atorvastatin across MDR1-MDCKII monolayers: efflux ratio 8.92. The authors later conclude that atorvastatin appears to be a transported substrate of P-gp.
In mild-moderate hypoxia (PO2 33–55 mm Hg, SAO2 65–91%), the BUI for 2-deoxy-D-glucose was 65.48 ± 2.99, not significantly different from control (NS).

Compound 57 (R=3-(difluoromethoxy)phenyl) was tested in LLC-PK1 cells transfected with human MDR1 (P-gp) at 1 µM concentration. The efflux ratio (B to A)/(A to B) was 49. The Papp AB in the parental cell line was 16 ×10−6 cm/s.
Phenytoin exhibits a brain/plasma ratio averaging 1.5, with corresponding brain concentrations between 60 and 120 µM.
